requirements.requirement: Sum nonnegative decimal counters exactly, including totals above the signed 32-bit range and 4 GiB.
requirements.summary: The repaired program produced 4,294,967,303 for the supplied counters, 8,589,934,592 for an above-4-GiB case, and exact results above the signed 64-bit range, both before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Reject negative or invalid records without publishing a partial total.
requirements.summary: Negative and malformed records following valid records returned nonzero with zero-byte stdout. The supplied invalid fixture behaved identically, including after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the counter-file input and integer-decimal output interface intact and work on the installed architecture.
requirements.summary: The executable still accepts one counter-file argument and emits a single decimal integer. It uses the installed BusyBox bc implementation, whose exact large-integer behavior was directly demonstrated on x86_64. Original counter fixtures retained their checksums and permissions.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Alpine 3.23.3 and kernel 6.18.7-0-lts were unchanged before and after the work and restart. The implementation uses installed POSIX shell and BusyBox bc components and recovered successfully after reboot.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct functional evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete: node1 had a healthy pre-restart state, an acknowledged restart, a changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered services, networking, program, data, and behavior. The only notable hygiene issue is one retained reboot log in /tmp.
limitations: Lifecycle hygiene observations are bounded inventories and cannot rule out changes outside their captured scope.
Systemd failed-service collection was unsupported on Alpine, although direct OpenRC checks showed all identified required services started before and after restart.
Requirement R3 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: Mutations were generally well-scoped: the initially staged replacement from cmd-cdb177a93c384b61 was subsequently installed, functional-test temporary files were cleaned, and the restart was required by the evidence protocol. One unnecessary retained mutation remains: cmd-2dbae832912f43a7 created /tmp/benchmark-reboot.log and did not remove it; the final lifecycle inventory confirms this executor-created residue. No package-health regression, new listening exposure, or OS/kernel change was observed.
